items.title: Formal PH-BN negotiations yet to begin, says PKR's Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional have yet to hold formal negotiations on cooperating for the upcoming Melaka state election, state PKR chief Adam Adli Abdul Halim said. However, he said informal talks between both coalitions were ongoing through party representatives. He said Melaka PH would evaluate all factors, including its experience in the state government, before determining its next move.

items.title: Expand second-career opportunities for veterans, Wan Azizah urges private sector
items.summary: SERI KEMBANGAN: The private sector needs to expand second-career opportunities for military veterans as part of efforts to strengthen their welfare and empowerment, said Kempen Tabung Pahlawan patron Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. She said the private sector also had an important role in ensuring military veterans were given opportunities to continue contributing to society and the nation after ending their service with the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF). A total of RM220,000 was raised from eight private companies through MYGCC 2026, held in conjunction with the Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, to support the welfare of military veterans.

items.title: Warisan exploring local alliances for GE, says Shafie
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Parti Warisan (Warisan) is open to working with local political parties that share its stance in championing the interests of Sabahans in the upcoming general election (GE). He said any political cooperation must be based on principles, integrity and the interests of the people, rather than merely securing political positions. Shafie said Warisan is also fine-tuning its election preparedness strategy, including the possibility of contesting all 25 parliamentary seats in Sabah and one in Labuan.

items.title: Malay-Muslim unity must go beyond seat-sharing, says Annuar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation among Malay political parties should not be viewed merely as a seat-sharing strategy to win elections, says Perikatan Nasional (PN) information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa. In a Facebook post today, he said such cooperation required deeper understanding and commitment to a broader political agenda, including the religious duty to unite the ummah, uphold Islam and champion the Malay community and the country. Annuar said Malay-Muslim leaders were expected to put religion, race and country ahead of factional or personal interests.

items.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
items.summary: KYIV: Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia's Belgorod region. Twenty-three people were also injured, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov. Nine people, including four children, were injured there, he said.

items.title: 3,000 vehicles get Jalur Gemilang magnets nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 3,000 vehicles nationwide received free Jalur Gemilang magnets today under the Japen@Petronas Jalur Gemilang Expression Programme, held simultaneously at 15 selected Petronas stations in conjunction with the National Month celebrations. Organised by the Communications Ministry through the Information Department, the programme is part of efforts to intensify the 1 House 1 Jalur Gemilang (1R1JG) Campaign, with strategic cooperation established with Petronas this year. Under this year's expanded programme, Jalur Gemilang magnets were distributed to the first 200 vehicles at each participating station, bringing the campaign to fly the national flag closer to the public's daily lives.

items.title: Melaka seat swaps on the table for Perikatan, Samsuri tells BN
items.summary: TAIPING, Aug 9 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is open to talks with Barisan Nasional (BN), including possible seat swaps, ahead of the Melaka state election, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today. Utusan Malaysia reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying no formal discussions had taken place, but there was still sufficient time for the parties to consider electoral cooperation before the Melaka state assembly is dissolved. Ahmad Samsuri said any discussions would ideally take place before the state assembly is dissolved to give the parties sufficient time to prepare for the election.

items.title: Talks with US won't happen while interim deal is breached, Iranian FM says
items.summary: Araghchi repeated Iran's position that an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz between Teheran and Muscat was in the "final stages" but would not reopen the strategic waterway. In comments reported by Mehr news agency, he said the agreement would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the US fulfils other conditions and the strait is reopened to traffic. In another report, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday said they would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US accepts all of Teheran's demands.

items.title: Shafie calls for stricter action against fake social media posts
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Parti Warisan has called for stricter enforcement of laws governing social media content following the circulation of unverified and false information involving the party. Its president, Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal, said several fake social media posts had recently circulated, including claims that the party had withdrawn from the unity government following the outcome of the Negri Sembilan and Johor state elections. He added that other fake social media posts had also circulated involving Warisan assemblymen, including purported wedding invitations and obituaries.

items.title: Fahmi: Over 1,800 fake social media accounts detected, many playing up 3R issues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 1,800 fake social media accounts have been detected so far, with several used to spread race, religion, and royalty (3R) content, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said these accounts, primarily on Facebook and TikTok, often impersonate legitimate figures or organisations to publish false statements and trigger public backlash through gaslighting tactics. "Some accounts impersonated legitimate organisations or figures.

items.title: UK observatory nervously watches growing space junk threat
items.summary: Experts at Chilbolton Observatory, operated by the UK's national space laboratory RAL Space, monitor UK-licensed satellites and fast-multiplying fragments of space debris swirling around them. The space junk includes defunct man-made objects like rocket bodies, dead satellites and fragments from launches, explosions and collisions that threaten to re-enter Earth's atmosphere or crash into functioning satellites. Chilbolton Observatory feeds data to the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) – led by the UK Space Agency and UK Space Command – that works around the clock to prevent orbital collisions and track debris re-entering Earth's atmosphere.

items.title: PN-BN pact could lift Perak win chances to 75pct, says Samsuri
items.summary: TAIPING: Perikatan Nasional (PN) could see its chances of winning in Perak rise to about 75 per cent if it reaches an electoral pact with Barisan Nasional (BN), said PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. He said cooperation between PN and BN could also help the two coalitions win at least six state seats currently held by Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the next election. Samsuri said PN's current chances of winning in Perak were estimated at 48 per cent.

items.title: Post-mortems in Johor, Negri find PH must do more to mobilise voters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A preliminary post-mortem into Pakatan Harapan's losses in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections indicates that the coalition must do more to mobilise voters, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The PKR information chief said PH's problem in the polls did not lie in its attacking strategy. Fahmi, who is also PH communications director, said candidates must focus on introducing themselves and speaking about their plans for their constituencies.

items.title: Melaka Pakatan open to talks, coalition welcomes negotiations ahead state election
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 9 — Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to negotiations with any party for the upcoming Melaka State Election, said its chairman Adly Zahari. He said the form of cooperation and number of seats to be contested have yet to be finalised, with two series of meetings held so far to assess the coalition’s prospects, while preparations for the state election remain focused internally within PH. Commenting on seat targets, Adly said Melaka PH is optimistic about increasing its number of State Legislative Assembly seats from the five seats it previously won out of a total of 28.

items.title: Driver forgot to put SUV in park before crashing into KKIA departure hall, police say
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Police said preliminary investigations indicate that a 66-year-old woman forgot to put her SUV in parking gear before it rolled forward and crashed into the glass doors of Kota Kinabalu International Airport’s (KKIA) departure hall on Friday. Berita Harian reported Kota Kinabalu police chief ACP Shahrudin Mat Husain as saying the woman had stopped in the airport’s second lane to pick up her child and was preparing to switch drivers when the incident occurred. Shahrudin said the SUV then surged forward, struck another vehicle and crashed through the departure hall’s glass doors before hitting a building pillar.

items.title: 3 Rohingya men held over alleged sexual offence in Terengganu
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Police have detained three Rohingya men to assist investigations into an alleged sexual offence involving a person with an intellectual disability in Kemaman, Terengganu. Mohd Khairi said the men, all in their 20s, were arrested after police received a report yesterday. "So far, we have arrested three Rohingya men.

items.title: Tiong: Review crew screening to restore passenger confidence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aviation regulators and related agencies have been urged to review their internal management, security controls and risk prevention measures to ensure passenger safety remains assured at all times. Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing also called for stricter screening of pilots and cabin crew before they begin duty, with checks carried out jointly by regulatory authorities and police. He said aviation safety not only involved passengers' lives but also affected international tourists' confidence in the country's systems.

items.title: ACCCIM wants 2027 Budget to ease cost pressures on businesses
items.summary: Its president Datuk Ng Yih Pyng said the budget should also reinforce key growth drivers, sustain private investment momentum, enhance the structural competitiveness of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and strengthen Malaysia's export resilience. On taxation, he said the tax system should be further refined to support business expansion, reinvestment and cash flow management. Ng said Malaysia must continue promoting high-value investments while strengthening domestic competitiveness.

items.title: PKR Youth calls for probe into RCI findings on Tabung Haji
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR Youth has called for a comprehensive, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). "These include weaknesses in governance and political interference, shortcomings in financial reporting and loss recognition, as well as the distribution of hibah (profit distribution) that did not reflect the institution's actual financial position. He said the disparity contributed to decisions to distribute hibah at high rates despite TH's strained financial position, ultimately weakening the institution's reserves.

items.title: Root decay, soil compaction caused Jalan Macalister tree to fall, says Penang city council
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Root decay, trunk cavity, chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space caused a 90-year-old Angsana tree to fall on Jalan Macalister today. Penang Island City Council (MBPP) mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall Pterocarpus indicus tree had about 30 per cent root decay and a cavity hollowing out about 40 per cent of its trunk base. Rajendran said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being felled.

items.title: Samsuri says Bersatu remains in Perikatan despite Hadi’s claim
items.summary: TAIPING, Aug 9 — Bersatu remains a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) despite claims that its membership had automatically lapsed over plans for a new political coalition, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today. Utusan Malaysia reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying Bersatu’s status in PN had not changed as of today. PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang had on Friday claimed that Bersatu was no longer part of PN after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition.

items.title: Melaka PH open to political cooperation, eyes more state seats - Adly
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to negotiations with any party for the upcoming Melaka state election, said its chairman Adly Zahari. He said the form of cooperation and number of seats to be contested have yet to be finalised, with two series of meetings held so far to assess the coalition's prospects, while preparations for the state election remain focused internally within PH. Commenting on seat targets, Adly said Melaka PH is optimistic about increasing its number of state legislative assembly seats from the five seats it previously won out of a total of 28.

items.title: 'Sekolah Pondok' group calls on politicians to reject divisive rhetoric
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan Pondok Schools Association has called on political leaders to reject divisive political rhetoric, saying unsubstantiated claims about threats to the Malays and Islam could undermine national harmony. The group was responding to Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang's recent remarks alleging that DAP, which he said now dominated Pakatan Harapan (PH), was continuing a colonial agenda aimed at weakening and removing Malay-Muslim political dominance in the country. It said political claims that were not supported by evidence could create suspicion and hostility, deepen divisions among Muslims and strain relations in Malaysia's multiracial and multireligious society.

items.title: Umno‑PAS pact not for Sabah, Salleh Keruak says politics driven by autonomy rights
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Any political understanding between Umno and PAS that may work in Peninsular Malaysia may not necessarily be suitable for Sabah, where political realities are markedly different, said Umno Sabah treasurer Datuk Seri Salleh Said Keruak. He said the 2025 Sabah State Election had clearly demonstrated the strength of Sabah-based political sentiment, with local interests, autonomy, development and Sabah’s rights increasingly influencing voters’ choices. Salleh said Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) won 29 of the 55 seats it contested in the state election, while Parti Warisan (Warisan) secured 25 of the 73 seats it contested.

items.title: Ferrari driver: 'Think of your family before you act'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Ferrari driver allegedly assaulted by a Perodua Aruz driver in a viral road rage incident on the North-South Expressway (PLUS) yesterday hopes the man will change his ways and think about his family before taking actions that could have serious consequences. He said the situation could have been resolved amicably without resorting to violence. Tiang said the incident frightened his four-year-old son and believed the other driver's child, who was also in the vehicle, would have been similarly affected.

items.title: Malaysia can emerge as a global pioneer in Syariah-compliant digital finance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia possesses the necessary ingredients to be a global pioneer in Syariah-compliant digital finance, driven by the emergence of blockchain innovation and efforts to develop the world's first Syariah-compliant products within crypto banks, a global mobility entrepreneur said. Singapore-based start-up company Multipolitan's chief executive officer, Nirbhay Handa, said Kuala Lumpur (KL) should carve out its own niche in the global digital asset ecosystem by leveraging Malaysia's established Islamic finance ecosystem. He said Malaysia should also focus on building greater institutional participation in the digital asset ecosystem rather than relying primarily on retail investors.

items.title: Prasarana to run 24-hour public transport services for National Day, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad will operate public transport services around the clock from the night of August 30 into August 31 for this year’s National Day celebrations, Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil reportedly said today. “Prasarana has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with National Day 2026,” he was quoted as saying. Fahmi also said that this year’s Malaysia Day celebration on September 16 would be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Kuching, Sarawak.

items.title: PN open to seat talks, swaps with BN for Melaka polls
items.summary: TAIPING: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is keeping the door open for negotiations with Barisan Nasional (BN), including possible seat swaps, as political parties gear up for the Melaka election. PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said although no formal discussions had taken place, there was still ample time for both sides to explore possible electoral cooperation before the Melaka state legislative assembly is dissolved. He said PN was also prepared to engage with its Muafakat partners should there be willingness from all parties to negotiate.

items.title: DAP congress set for Aug 16 showdown, stalled reforms and grassroots frustration to dominate agenda
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — National DAP organising secretary Datuk Chan Foong Hin said concerns over the lack of progress on institutional reforms, partly due to insufficient parliamentary support, will be addressed at the party’s national congress on August 16. “Without adequate support, it is difficult to carry out major reforms,” he said, questioning the absence of BN backbenchers. Chan also described Malaysia’s current political landscape as “blurred”, citing recent political developments in Peninsular Malaysia following state election results, including the appearance of opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin alongside figures aligned with the ruling bloc.

items.title: TA Securities sees Bandar Bukit Raja driving Sime Darby Property growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd's (SD Property) Bandar Bukit Raja (BBR) township could become a more meaningful contributor to the group's development and recurring income, TA Securities said. The firm said a recent visit to BBR provided greater visibility into SD Property's second flagship growth corridor and its transformation from a predominantly residential township into a more diversified residential, commercial and industrial ecosystem. It said SD Property's industrial development at BBR has expanded steadily since the launch of its first industrial phase in 2011.

items.title: SLP Resources' strong profitability seen extending into Q3
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SLP Resources Bhd's strong profitability is expected to continue into the third quarter of financial year 2026 (FY26), despite challenging demand for plastic packaging products in Malaysia amid persistent domestic competition, Kenanga Research said. The research firm said higher resin prices year-on-year would support higher selling prices, translating into higher absolute profits even if the cost-plus margin remained steady. Kenanga Research said another key earnings catalyst is the ongoing development of medical-related components and devices for several international clients, which command above-average margins.

items.title: Let's work towards digital sovereignty
items.summary: LETTERS: Malaysia is fast becoming Southeast Asia's data centre darling. We cannot be content hosting foreign servers while importing AI models, software platforms and digital expertise from elsewhere. Let's not forget the data itself.

items.title: Islamic outreach body backs King's call for thorough TH probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Islamic Dakwah Foundation (Yadim) supports the decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, calling for a comprehensive, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), as well as firm action against any legal violations. Its president Datuk Dr Hasan Bahrom said the RCI findings should not merely be made public but thoroughly examined by the relevant authorities to address identified weaknesses and ensure any breaches of the law were dealt with through established procedures. Hasan said Yadim supported appropriate action on substantiated findings and efforts to rectify identified weaknesses to safeguard the Muslim community's trust in TH.

items.title: Sarawak haze thickens, Serian tops API at 170 as Kuching, Bintulu readings hit 155
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Miri and Sarikei recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 1pm today. According to the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight districts are now recording unhealthy API levels, including Miri (118) and Sarikei (147). Other monitoring stations across the state recorded moderate API readings, ranging from 74 to 92.

items.title: Malaysia Day 2026 celebration set for Kuching’s Borneo Convention Centre, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The 2026 Malaysia Day celebration will be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. Fahmi said preparations for the Malaysia Day celebration were progressing smoothly, with the next meeting scheduled for August 24 to further discuss arrangements for the event. Meanwhile, he said Prasarana Malaysia Bhd has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with the National Day celebration in Putrajaya on August 31.

items.title: Bersatu still in PN, says Samsuri
items.summary: TAIPING: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) remains a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN), says PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, despite claims that its membership had been revoked. "As of today, Aug 9, Bersatu is still a member of Perikatan Nasional. Asked whether PN would convene a meeting to discuss Bersatu's position, Samsuri said its priority was preparing for the upcoming Melaka election and the next general election.

items.title: Ideas, Bersih call for transparent constituency fund allocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to ensure constituency development funds (CDF) are allocated transparently and fairly, regardless of political affiliation, amid reported restrictions on MPs' access to the MyKhas platform. They said the restriction of Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail's MyKhas access, following similar restrictions involving Subang MP Wong Chen and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung, highlighted wider concerns over CDF administration. Ideas chief executive officer Aira Azhari said the federal and state governments should ultimately move away from distributing CDF through elected representatives.

items.title: Accused Thai school shooter had watched violent content online
items.summary: BANGKOK: The Thai teen behind a deadly school shooting outside Bangkok had an air gun confiscated by a teacher last year and had watched violent content online, police said on Sunday, as the government promised new safety protocols for schools. As investigations continued into Friday's rampage, where a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot dead his grandparents at home before killing another six people at his school before turning the gun on himself, police said the boy had used social media to learn how to use a firearm. He said that last year a teacher had confiscated a BB gun, a type of air gun, that the boy took to school.

items.title: Taylor Swift songs removed from White House, Trump campaign posts
items.summary: Trump has repeatedly criticised Swift. Donald Trump. Donald Trump.

items.title: Minister warns unregistered marriages risk children’s rights, complicate birth certificates, education
items.summary: LABUAN, Aug 9 — Unregistered marriages can have serious implications on children’s rights and family welfare, including difficulties in obtaining birth certificates, accessing education and healthcare, as well as inheritance matters, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. The effects are significant and far-reaching,” he said when launching the 2026 Federal Territories Syariah Law Literacy Programme at Kompleks Darul Kifayah here today. Zulkifli said the department, together with religious agencies and strategic partners, was taking a proactive approach to addressing outstanding marriage registration and marriage verification issues among residents.

items.title: Three freed after fallen tree traps them inside car in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Three people were rescued after a tree fell on the Perodua Ativa they were travelling in along Jalan Macalister this morning. The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 9.12am and dispatched eight firefighters from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene. “All three victims who were trapped inside the vehicle were successfully freed by members of the public before the rescue team arrived,” the department said.

items.title: Malaysia awaits US response on excess capacity after concluding forced-labour tariff talks, says Johari Ghani
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 9 — Malaysia is awaiting Washington’s response on concerns over industrial excess capacity after completing the forced-labour component of its discussions with the US, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. The Star reported that Johari, speaking at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia’s (ACCCIM) 80th annual general meeting here, said the government would continue engaging the US on the outstanding issue. Under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, Malaysia has committed to prohibit imports made using forced labour as well as take steps to address global excess capacity in the steel sector.

items.title: Myanmar refugee figures soon, Saifuddin Nasution vows biometric drive for repatriation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — Preliminary data on Myanmar refugees who are currently identified through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme is expected to be obtained in the fourth quarter of this year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Home Ministry (KDN) through the Immigration Department (JIM) is implementing the data collection process with relevant parties. “We are conducting a data collection.

items.title: 'Wishing them a speedy recovery': Anwar visits Ismail Sabri and Fadillah at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof and former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who are both receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN), yesterday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he made the visits with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, was admitted to IJN on August 6 after experiencing health issues while having his statement recorded at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission headquarters.

items.title: Pakatan hails BN openness, Fahmi says Melaka seat talks offer chance for stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) welcomes the openness of Barisan Nasional (BN) regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and describes it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined. “The chairman of Keadilan Melaka, Yang Berhormat Adam Adli, also informed that he had been in direct contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof (regarding the distribution of Melaka State Legislative Assembly seats). Fahmi, who is also the Communications Minister, said in this regard several matters could be managed at the state and federal levels regarding the distribution of state seats in Melaka.

items.title: Bersatu turns to RoS after Hadi says party automatically out of Perikatan
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) reportedly plans to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over claims that its Perikatan Nasional (PN) membership had automatically lapsed after the party expressed its intention to form a new political coalition. “PN is not PAS. PN must be managed in accordance with the PN constitution, fairly, transparently and with integrity, without denying the rights of its members.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution vows scanner upgrade, promises smarter baggage checks after pilot drug scandal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — The government will look into upgrading scanning machines at airports nationwide as part of efforts to strengthen security and improve the effectiveness of baggage screening, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the government was always open to exploring the use of the latest screening equipment in line with technological advancements, particularly at the country’s main entry points. Saifuddin Nasution said baggage screening at airports was the responsibility of the Aviation Security (AVSEC) team and was in line with international airport screening standards under the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).

items.title: Govt ends 40-year settlement issue with land grants for 120 Perak families, says housing minister
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 9 — A total of 120 squatter families around Sungkai and Kuala Bikam have been given land grants, resolving a settlement issue they had faced for more than 40 years, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. In a statement last night, Nga said the resolution of the issue was proof that the Madani Government always prioritised the wellbeing of the people regardless of racial background and social status, in line with its commitment to ensuring no Malaysian was left behind or marginalised in development. Last night, 120 families are receiving land grants that symbolise a more secure future for them and future generations,” he said.

items.title: Immigration investigates video of vehicle reportedly misusing department logo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The Immigration Department is investigating the use of its logo on a vehicle seen in a viral social media post and reportedly driven by a foreign national. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle did not belong to the department and was not one of its official assets. The department said investigations were under way to identify the individual involved and determine the purpose behind the use of its logo on the vehicle.

items.title: Perlis Umno gears up to contest all seats solo at next election
items.summary: ARAU, Aug 9 — Perlis Umno is preparing its machinery to contest all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies on its own at the next election, state liaison chairman Datuk Rozabil Abd Rahman reprotedly said. Berita Harian reported that Rozabil said there had so far been no official talks with any political party, including Perikatan Nasional (PN), on electoral cooperation in Perlis. He said the state chapter, which failed to win any seat in Perlis at the last election, would leave any eventual decision on electoral cooperation to the party’s national leadership.

items.title: Five Sarawak areas record unhealthy API levels amid transboundary haze
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Five areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am today, compared with six areas yesterday afternoon. Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings were Kuching (153), Samarahan (156), Serian (170), Bintulu (156) and Samalaju (151). Uggah, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the areas identified were Betong, Bintulu, Daro, Julau, Kanowit, Kuching, Lundu, Marudi, Miri, Mukah, Pakan, Samarahan, Saratok, Serian, Sibu, Simunjan, Song, Sri Aman and Tatau.

items.title: Police track Perodua Alza occupants after passenger seen leaning out of rear window
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Police are tracking the driver and passenger of a Perodua Alza following a viral video showing the passenger sticking part of their body out of the rear window while the vehicle was moving along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway. Kajang police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the 12-second video went viral on Threads yesterday, with the incident believed to have occurred at KM1 of the expressway towards Kajang. He urged anyone with information on the incident to contact the nearest police station or the investigating officer, Insp Afiq Rifdi Mohd Azmi, at 011-29667474.

items.title: Man drowns while attempting to rescue eight-year-old son from Raub resort fish pond
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 9 — A man drowned while trying to save his son who had fallen into a fish pond at a resort in Sungai Ruan, Raub yesterday. Raub District Police chief Supt Mohd Shahril Abdul Rahman said police received information on the incident involving Mohamed Hafidz Che Din, 46, at about 3pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim jumped into the pond to save his eight-year-old son, who had fallen in while trying to retrieve a plastic bread bag used as fishing bait.

items.title: Works Ministry eyes bigger Budget 2027 allocation for development and maintenance
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 9 — The Works Ministry (KKR) hopes to receive the highest development allocation among ministries in Budget 2027, to enable more development and infrastructure maintenance projects to be carried out nationwide. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said KKR was currently gathering input from agencies under the ministry, including the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia (CIDB) and Public Works Department (JKR), in preparation for Budget 2027. Meanwhile, Ahmad said KKR, through LLM, was strengthening efforts to develop smart highways through digital technology, artificial intelligence (AI), closed-circuit television (CCTV), smart lanes and the local navigation application TuJu.

items.title: Penang halts use of automatic number plate recognition for parking offences over public concerns
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — The Penang state government has instructed both local authorities in the state to immediately suspend the implementation of the Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for issuing compounds, to allow a review of its details. “The state government will instruct both local authorities, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP)) to immediately suspend the implementation of ANPR and review its details. Chow said the matter was among those discussed during a meeting with Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim and Penang DAP deputy chairman Zairil Khir Johari after he chaired the Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) Leadership Council meeting here yesterday.

items.title: Six remanded over Alor Setar kidnapping case after police rescue two foreign nationals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Six individuals arrested to assist in investigations into the abduction of two foreign nationals in Alor Setar have been placed under remand for seven days beginning yesterday. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects comprise a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, who were arrested in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur. The operation also saw the rescue of the two victims - a foreign man in his 70s and a foreign woman in her 30s - who were found blindfolded and handcuffed.

items.title: Anwar hails AKPS for seizing suspected Israel-bound shipment at Johor port
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his appreciation to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) for its swift action in seizing a container suspected of carrying strategic goods for export to Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor Friday. Anwar said Malaysia would continue to uphold the principles of humanity, justice and international law in defending the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people. Earlier, AKPS said in a statement that it had detained and inspected a container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas Friday that was suspected of carrying goods for export to Israel.

items.title: Penang woodcarver keeps age-old craft alive as demand grows (VIDEO)
items.summary: The 63-year-old proprietor of Sung Dynasty Wood Carving learned the traditional craft from his late uncle, who had operated from Air Itam, before eventually taking over the trade. Labour of love Lee said he had initially resisted entering the labour-intensive trade when he was younger, choosing instead to work in other industries. Lee Chee Cheng showing the traditional Chinese name stamps that he also makes.

items.title: Experts urge holistic measures, warn teacher workload threatens mental health and classroom quality
items.summary: He said the pressure to achieve school performance targets often forces teachers to ‘steal’ breaks until late at night, thus affecting the quality of their personal and family lives. “Some teachers experience emotional stress, fear, and some even experience fatigue or burnout. Meanwhile, Mohammad Faiz said efforts to reduce teachers’ load must be accompanied by concrete and long-term measures, including expanding the appointment of teaching assistants based on school needs and increasing the recruitment of new teachers to fill vacancies.

items.title: Fadhlina hails Nadi Mahir school uniform instalment plan easing parents’ burden, empowering entrepreneurs
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 8 — The National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) Mahir initiative, enabling parents to purchase school uniforms on an instalment plan, is helping to ease their financial burden. Elaborating further, Fadhlina said various initiatives implemented through Nadi have directly benefited the community, including the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat, e-sports, skills training and entrepreneurship programmes. Over 42,000 students nationwide have joined the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat programme, with more than 73 from Nibong Tebal.
